reference: GNU coreutils cat from the runner's reference PATH, with LC_ALL=C and TZ=UTC. Each parity case runs the identical Bash script first against GNU cat and then against the candidate with an empty PATH; the runner compares status, stdout bytes, stderr policy, and fixture tree. The separate metadata contract uses Bash's type/help builtins and the cat_doc text in the pinned implementation; it is not operation parity.
coverage: Binary concatenation across files, including NUL and high bytes, with redirected output and resulting file contents.
Line numbering across operands, -b precedence over -n, and the documented --number-nonblank alias.
Blank-line squeezing across file boundaries and trailing partial lines.
-A visible rendering of control, tab, newline, DEL, and high-bit bytes in the C locale.
-- option termination, option-like filenames, and '-' reading redirected standard input between files.
Continuation after multiple ordinary missing-file errors, plus rejection of an invalid option.
Sequential invocations using distinct redirected stdin files in one shell.
exclusions: This suite samples the documented common GNU interface and does not claim full GNU cat option parity.

Output write-error propagation and same-shell recovery are deferred because the safe runner does not expose a private failing output device; they require a disposable VM with a private failure sink or an independently reviewed write/close syscall mock.
No terminal-specific behavior or host device paths are exercised.

cases.purpose: Concatenate two small binary files without inserting separators, write the result to a relative output file, and emit that file; verify bytes and all file effects against GNU cat.
cases.script: printf 'A\000B\n' > left; printf '\377tail' > right; cat left right > joined; cat joined

cases.purpose: Compare -A rendering of control bytes, a tab, a newline, DEL, and high-bit bytes under the runner's C locale.
Check that -- makes -n and -- literal filenames while '-' reads redirected stdin at its position between file operands.
cases.script: printf 'dash-n\000\n' > -n; printf 'dash-dash\n' > --; printf 'stdin\377' > input; cat -- -n - -- < input

cases.purpose: Check that ordinary open failures set a failing status and emit diagnostics while cat still copies a valid operand between them.
cases.script: printf 'survivor\000\n' > present; cat missing-first present missing-last

cases.purpose: Check rejection of an unsupported option with a nonzero status and diagnostic.
Check two cat invocations in one shell read distinct redirected files and concatenate their contents without stale or lost input.
cases.script: printf 'first\n' > one; printf 'second\000tail' > two; cat < one; cat < two

cases.purpose: Verify Bash reports cat as a builtin and that help has an entry, without treating metadata as cat operation coverage.
cases.script: if [[ $(type -t cat) == builtin ]] && help cat > metadata.out; then printf 'builtin\nhelp\n'; else exit 1; fi

cases.purpose: Qualify cat's stdout write-error status and the shell's ability to continue after the error.
Reject a regular input file that is also the append-mode output file; retain original bytes and compare the diagnostic/status with GNU cat.
A directory read error must not prevent copying a later regular operand.
cases.script:
mkdir folder
printf 'after\n' > present
cat folder present

cases.purpose: An ordinary closed stdout redirection must fail and diagnose; the next invocation in the same shell must write normally.
cases.script:
printf 'one\n' > input
if cat input >&-; then exit 90; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
cat input
